newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end firmer on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end firmer on foreign buying.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks closed firmer on Tuesday as foreign investors celebrated the Liberal Party's re-election with a majority government. * 93 million shares traded worth C$1.4 million.
Toronto stocks closed firmer on Tuesday as foreign investors snapped up Canadian issues after the ruling Liberals secured another majority government in Monday's federal election.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 26.64 points to close at 6432.72. Total volume was 93.3 million shares worth C$1.4 billion.
Despite winning a bare majority, foreign investors cheered the Liberal victory as a sign that the government's deficit reduction program would continue, traders said.
"From a foreigner's perspective, it's a majority government," said Maison Placements Canada trader Rolie Bradley. "The game plan continues."
Bradley added that stocks with the largest market value led the Canadian market higher.
Eleven of Toronto's 14 sub-sectors gained ground, led by banks, conglomerates, consumer products, media and utilities. The three weak groups were golds, industrial products and transportation.
Advancing stocks outnumbered declines 509 to 447, while 290 issues were flat.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Stelco Inc topped Toronto's most-active list and closed steady at 10.35 on 3.4 million shares.
Algoma Steel Inc followed in heavy trading, up 0.25 at 9.05. Investors were betting that a stronger economy will boost demand for steel by manufacturers, analysts said.
* Telecommunications conglomerate BCE Inc, Canada's largest publicly traded firm, rose 0.80 to 38.00.

* Inco Ltd gained 0.25 to close at 44.65 after its Sudbury workers rejected a contract offer and walked off the job. The production shutdown caused a brief rally in nickel prices which boosted Inco's stock, analysts said.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109))
